title noun

of a book, poem or work

also titles, book title, entitled, be called (of a book), title tag, heading

classical

Ov. Rem. 1: titulum nōmenque libellī (Lewis & Short)

Traupman 326

titulus, titulī m.

noun, second declension

title (of a book); label, notice

The usual word for a book’s title from Augustus on. Lewis & Short’s other senses: an inscription or epitaph, a label on a jar or a slave put up for sale, a notice that a house is for sale or to let (Plin. Ep. 7.27.7), and, figuratively, a title of honour (see title, of a person) or a pretext.

Other words

  • īnscrīptiō, īnscrīptiōnis f. — title (what is written on a book); an inscription

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 16.11.4; Traupman 395; M-O s.v. title (of book, article)

    Cicero’s word for the title of his De officiis. Properly “a writing on”, so also an inscription on a monument (Plin. NH 29.11) or a brand on a slave’s forehead (Petr.).

  • īnscrībō, īnscrībere, īnscrīpsī, īnscrīptum — to entitle; liber īnscrībitur, the book is called

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.31: quī īnscrībitur Laelius; M-O s.v. title (of book, article)

    Cicero’s way of giving a title: in eō librō, quī Oeconomicus īnscrībitur (Off. 2.87).

  • index, indicis m. — title; the title tag hung on a book roll

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Orat. 2.61: dēceptus indicibus librōrum (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 4.4a.1

    The strip of parchment that carried a roll’s title, Greek σίλλυβος (Cic. Att. 4.4a.1), and so the title itself (Suet. Cal. 49, Liv. 38.56). Its everyday senses are others: a pointer, the forefinger, an informer, a list (see index, in a book).

Examples

  • Sed dē amīcitiā aliō librō dictum est, quī īnscrībitur Laelius.

    But friendship has been dealt with in another book, which is entitled Laelius.Cic. Off. 2.31

  • quod dē īnscrīptiōne quaeris, nōn dubitō quīn καθῆκον officium sit, nisi quid tū aliud; sed īnscrīptiō plēnior dē officiīs.

    As for your question about the title: I have no doubt that καθῆκον is officium, unless you think otherwise; but the fuller title is De officiis.Cic. Att. 16.11.4

  • iīsque imperēs ut sūmant membrānulam ex quā indicēs fīant, quōs vōs Graecī, ut opīnor, σιλλύβους appellātis.

    and tell them to get a bit of parchment to make the title tags, which you Greeks, I think, call sillyboi.Cic. Att. 4.4a.1

See also book, index, title, author.
